items.summary: We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding. To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that ret…
items.curatorExcerpt: We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding. To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks. Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit): - DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6 - Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4 - AIME 25+26: 97.7 / 98.3 / 96.5 / 86.0 - MSGM: 94.0 / 93.1 / 91.8 / 90.6 - RealWorldQA: 82.4 / 82.4 / 81.3 / 80.9 Decode speed is comparable to other quants on an RTX PRO 6000. Context-length results below (3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit / Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS): - 4K: 88.9 / 99.2 / 111.7 / 94.7 - 16K: 84.5 / 93.8 / 105.1 / 89.8 - 64K: 70.7 / 77.5 / 85.0 / 74.8 Running these currently require our llama.cpp fork: ( https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp ) Feedback and questions welcome. We'd love to hear how these perform on your workloads.

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.summary: Using agent teams and formal verification to improve quantum algorithms for fusion and chemistry.
items.detailExcerpt: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg and Ryan Babbush How using agent teams and formal verification can improve quantum algorithms for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes Quantum computers could soon solve problems beyond the reach of classical supercomputers. However, there is a catch: even when using the best quantum algorithms, some important applications still require more resources than early quantum hardware will be able to support. In a new paper , we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits. These optimized circuits, which are instructions for how a quantum computer should carry out an algorithm, could one day help us run simulations that solve complex scientific challenges, from fusion energy to drug design. To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library , problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub.

items.summary: 🔥🔥🔥 Open-source Jira, Linear, Monday, and ClickUp alternative. Plane is a modern project management platform to manage tasks, sprints, docs, and triage.
items.detailExcerpt: Modern project management for all teams Website • Forum • X • Documentation Meet Plane, an open-source project management tool to track issues, run ~sprints~ cycles, and manage product roadmaps without the chaos of managing the tool itself. 🧘‍♀️ Plane is evolving every day. Your suggestions, ideas, and reported bugs help us immensely. Do not hesitate to join in the conversation on Forum or raise a GitHub issue. We read everything and respond to most. 🚀 Installation Getting started with Plane is simple. Choose the setup that works best for you: • Plane Cloud Sign up for a free account on Plane Cloud—it's the fastest way to get up and running without worrying about infrastructure. • Self-host Plane Prefer full control over your data and infrastructure? Install and run Plane on your own servers. Follow our detailed deployment guides to get started. Installation methods Docs link -------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Docker Kubernetes All-in-one Docker deployments/aio/community · docs Instance admins can configure instance settings with God mode. 🌟 Features • Work Items Efficiently create and manage tasks with a robust rich text editor that supports file uploads. Enhance organization and tracking by adding sub-properties and referencing related issues. • Cycles Maintain your team’s momentum with Cycles. Track progress effortlessly using burn-down charts and other insightful tools. • Modules Simplify complex projects by dividing them into smaller, manageable modules. • Views Customize your workflow by creating filters to display only the most relevant issues. Save and share these views with ease. • Pages Capture and organize ideas using Plane Pages, complete with AI capabilities and a rich text editor. Format text, insert images, add hyperlinks, or convert your notes into actionable items. • Analytics Access real-time insights across all your Plane data. Visualize trends, remove blockers, and keep your projects moving forward. 🛠️ Local development See CONTRIBUTING ⚙️ Built with 📸 Screenshots 📝 Documentation Explore Plane's product documentation and developer documentation to learn about features, setup, and usage. ❤️ Community Join the Plane community on our Forum, and use GitHub issues for bug reports and feature requests. We follow a Code of conduct in all our community channels. Feel free to ask questions, report bugs, participate in discussions, share ideas, request features, or showcase your projects. We’d love to hear from you! 🛡️ Security If you discover a security vulnerability in Plane, please report it responsibly instead of opening a public issue. We take all legitimate reports seriously and will investigate them promptly. See Security policy for more info. To disclose any security issues, please report them privately on GitHub or email us at security@plane.so. 🤝 Contributing There are many ways you can contribute to Plane: • Report bugs or submit feature requests. • Review the documentation and tell us on the Forum or in a GitHub issue where it is wrong or incomplete. • Add or update translations. • Talk or write about Plane or any other ecosystem integration and let us know! • Show your support by upvoting popular feature requests. Please read CONTRIBUTING.md for details on the process for submitting pull requests to us. Repo activity We couldn't have done this without you.
